LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How would you get the total number of people in a group? 2. How do you tell the place value of a digit in a number?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to counting of numbers forward up to 1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. count numbers forward up to 1000 starting from any point.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. count numbers forward in multiples of 100 from 1000.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. identify the place value of numbers up to hundreds.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. read numbers 1- 1000 in symbols,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. read, write and sign numbers 1-100 in words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. identify missing numbers in number patterns up to 1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. play games involving number patterns up to 1000 ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign in 1’s, 10’s, and 100's starting from any point up to 1000. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to sign numbers forward in 1’s, 10’s, and 100’s starting from any point up to 1000 using rope skipping in a safe environment. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to practise through play using number cards counting numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to read by signing and identify place value up to hundreds using place value apparatus in class. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to watch signed videos/ captions/ pictures /charts on numbers 1-1000 then discuss and make notes. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to sign read numbers 1. How would you get the total number of people in a group? 2. How do you tell the place value of a digit in a number? 5 1-1000 in symbols starting from any point. ● In pairs or and taking turns to read by signing and write numbers 1-100 in words using number cards. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to create number patterns up to 1000 and share with other groups, post them on the wall or be attached to their individual portfolios. ● Learners are guided to play games involving whole numbers up to 1000 using digital devices and other resources. Core-Competence to be developed: ● Learning to learn: Independent learning skills as learners work on their own in assigned tasks of counting numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
